same_change.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. B makes A unnecessary: B already makes the change A makes (the same fix or the same addition, in essentially the same way, possibly as a slightly larger or smaller version of it), so once B is in, A adds nothing. Judge only from the titles, messages, file lists and diffs; ignore which branch either one targets.

builds_on.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. A depends on or follows B: A continues, extends, completes, fixes, or reverts B's change, so A only makes sense with B's change in mind. Answer low if the two are independent changes that merely touch the same code.

same_goal.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. A and B address the same bug, issue or feature, but by a different method: a different fix, a different design or a different part of the code, so they are alternatives rather than one change made twice. Answer low if they make essentially the same change, or if they address different problems.
